pages.text: "Bread is ready! I will eat in the yard!" Pipo picked up a warm piece. Mom said, "Pipo, sit down to eat." He was already rushing outside.
In the yard, one hand held bread, the other a wooden ball. Pipo took a bite and rolled the ball. Each run after it dropped crumbs. "Eating while running is more fun!"
"Pipo, a bread trail behind you!" Mrs. Goose called over the wall. He looked back: goslings followed in a line, pecking crumbs. Only a tiny bit of bread remained in his hand. "Oh? My bread!"
Mom hugged Pipo and settled him in a table chair. "Let us play. This chair is a sheep pen. Sit your bottom down, and the gate shuts!" His ears perked. "If it shuts, I cannot get out?"
Mom drew a circle around the chair with a finger. "Here is the pen gate—shut!" A little stone wall seemed to surround its legs. "My pen!" Pipo planted his bottom firmly.
Mom gave him bread and sang, "Bread at the table—yum!" She opened fingers one by one. "One, bottom stays! Two, both hands and yum! Three, finish, then open the gate!" He held bread with both hands.
Outside, goslings looked for crumbs. Pipo stayed firmly in his chair. Bread in both hands, one bite, two bites. "Bread at the table—yum!" Crumbs fell only on the table.
The plate was empty. "Open the pen gate!" Pipo hopped down. Outside, Mrs. Goose stretched her neck. "Not a crumb here!" Crouching with hands at his chest, he said, "Finished!"
Pipo knew the eating order. "One, bottom stays! Two, both hands and yum! Three, finish, then open the gate!" The next morning, at the sheep's baa, he slipped into his chair first.

Pipo drew Mom's hand toward the next chair. "Mom, sit and eat with me!" Eating at the table kept all the bread from getting lost. Resting his head on her shoulder, he called, "Bread at the table—yum!"
